solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Religious Education on page monks, say, reserve in advance

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it, so the religious letters come after the page letter

parts.note: RE is the school subject Religious Education
monks are an example of a religious order

explanation.surface: Someone books a religious text in advance, pictured as a schoolroom page about monks.
explanation.definitionFit: To place an order for goods before they are available is to book them ahead of time.

clue.text: Wash some gear in secret

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Doing a bit of laundry of one's kit on the quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse clothes is to wash them in clean water.

clue.text: Not worth considering boxing fight shunned by beginner

indicators.note: shunned by means the first letter is avoided, so it is dropped from the boxing match word

parts.note: a bout is a boxing contest
the beginner of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A boxing match avoided by a novice is not worth considering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginner' here is the first letter of BOUT, not a novice boxer; removing it leaves OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea that is out, as in out of the question, is ruled out and not worth considering.

clue.text: Speak slowly, attract learner

parts.note: to draw a crowd is to attract it
L is the learner driver plate

explanation.surface: A tutor talking slowly to attract a student.
explanation.definitionFit: To drawl is to talk in a slow, lazy way with drawn-out vowels.

clue.text: University staff referring to publicity at Queen's?

parts.note: RE means about or concerning
an ad is publicity for a product
ER is the Queen, Elizabeth Regina, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: Academics talking about advertising at Queen's University.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen's looks like the university in Belfast, but it gives ER plus S.
explanation.definitionFit: In British universities a reader is a senior academic rank just below professor.

clue.text: God! That's not half thorough

indicators.note: taking only half of the word thorough keeps its first four letters and discards the rest

explanation.surface: An exasperated exclamation that a job has been done only half-heartedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is also British slang for 'very much', which adds to the disguise; here it means take half of 'thorough'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse deity of thunder, wielder of the hammer Mjolnir, is a god.

clue.text: After time, inquire about supporting Church's specially-formed group

indicators.note: after means the inquiring phrase comes after the time letter
in a down clue, a piece supporting another sits beneath it, so the church letters go last

parts.note: to ask for someone is to inquire about them
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Later, someone asks about backing for a church's purpose-built committee.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit set up for a single mission or operation is a dedicated team of this kind.

clue.text: Love new lid on drink container

indicators.note: in a down clue the shuffled lid letters sit on top of the drink letters

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: new means the letters of lid are put in a fresh order

parts.note: rum is a spirit drink

explanation.surface: A sweetheart puts a new cap on a bottle of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A large metal barrel for storing fuel oil is a container.

clue.text: Small group not heard

indicators.note: heard tells us the word not is spoken and the entry is a word with the same sound

parts.note: the word is said aloud as written

explanation.surface: A remark that a few people went unheard.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cluster of people standing together is called a knot, as in a knot of onlookers.

clue.text: Mead? Alas, turns out to be water

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters of mead and alas end up arranged differently

explanation.surface: A drinker is disappointed to find the honey wine is only water.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is a jocular old idiom for plain drinking water, the only drink the first man had.

clue.text: It's legal, due, to change President

indicators.note: the letters of legal and due are to be changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that a law change is lawful and overdue.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles de Gaulle was President of France from 1959 to 1969.

clue.text: Main oar is repaired here in Turkey

indicators.note: repaired means fixed or remade, so the letters of main oar is are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A boat's chief oar gets mended somewhere in Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula of Anatolia, the Asian part of Turkey, was known historically by this name.

clue.text: Horse's previous record in class

definitions.meaning: a racehorse's past results are its ..., as printed in the racing pages
a school class or year group is a ... in British schools

explanation.surface: A racing tipster's look at how a horse has run in its class.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: racing results history, and a British school year group.

clue.text: I'm seen with Bible forsaking large drink

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: forsaking means abandoning, so a letter is dropped from the word Bible

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to appearing with a scripture while giving up heavy drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forsaking large' removes L from BIBLE, leaving BIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbibe is to drink, especially alcohol; both are verbs.

clue.text: From Guatemala, I sense a general problem

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the phrase that follows, running across its words

explanation.surface: A traveller senses a widespread problem in Guatemala.
explanation.definitionFit: A pervasive feeling of unease or decline, as in an economic slump, is a widespread ill.

clue.text: English politician at sports fixture's finding evidence of earlier drinking?

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
a tie is a sports fixture such as a cup tie, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: An English MP at a match is caught out by signs of drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty bottles and glasses left lying around show that the drink has been consumed.

clue.text: Fish in quiet river with mischievous child

parts.note: SH is the hushing call for quiet
an imp is a naughty child

explanation.surface: A naughty child angling in a quiet river.
explanation.definitionFit: A small crustacean caught and eaten as seafood, loosely counted as fish on menus.

clue.text: At outset positive, look up manager's description of well-paid job

indicators.note: at the outset of each word means the opening letters of positive, look, up and manager's are taken

explanation.surface: Advice to stay upbeat and consult the boss's account of a lucrative role.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum job or plum post is an idiom for a highly desirable, lucrative position.

clue.text: Spy sabre, exotic, for witness?

indicators.note: exotic means strange or unusual, so the letters of spy and sabre are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A secret agent with a foreign sword, needed in a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone happening to walk past an incident may be its only onlooker and observer.

clue.text: Transparent fabric? Absolutely

definitions.meaning: a very fine, see-through material such as a stocking
utter or complete, as in a total waste

explanation.surface: A shop assistant confirms that a fabric is see-through.
explanation.definitionFit: One word for fine see-through cloth and for utter or complete, as in pure nonsense.

clue.text: Graduate's home sink

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate, and the 's adds S
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A student's house has a kitchen sink.
explanation.definitionFit: A washbasin is a bowl for washing in, just as a sink is.

clue.text: On return Gibraltar number one's with European, important person

indicators.note: on return means the short form for Gibraltar is read backwards

parts.note: GIB is the common short name for Gibraltar
one is I, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A dignitary comes home to Gibraltar as the top man along with a European.
explanation.definitionFit: A big noise is an informal idiom for a person of influence, a VIP or bigwig.

clue.text: Think she has eight sisters — heavenly!

definitions.meaning: each of the nine goddesses of the arts in Greek myth has eight sisters, and they are divine

explanation.surface: Someone imagines a woman blessed with eight sisters and finds it wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavenly!' looks like an exclamation of delight but tells you the sister is a goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Ponder and reflect are synonyms of the verb; the nine daughters of Zeus inspired the arts.

clue.text: Dull, impact oddly lacking

indicators.note: oddly lacking means the odd-numbered letters of impact go missing, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A dreary effect which strangely lacks punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A mat or matt finish has no shine, so it is lustreless or flat.

clue.text: Breed behind tower

definitions.meaning: to breed animals is to raise them
to tower is to rise up high, as a horse or a cliff does

explanation.surface: Three apparently unconnected words: a breed of animal behind a tower.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers raising animals, the back part or backside, and rising up high.

clue.text: Close examination of Southern vineyard, very small

parts.note: a cru is a French vineyard or its wine
tiny means very small

explanation.surface: A wine buff inspects a tiny vineyard in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrutiny is careful, critical inspection of something.
